course.title: Electrical Installation Basics
course.tagline: Wire lights, sockets and panels safely, and fault-find like a pro.

days.title: How Electricity Works in Your Home
days.goal: Follow electricity from the street pole to a socket in your home.

video.title: How Electricity Works in Your House (From the Pole to Your Outlet)

steps: Learn that power comes from the street into a meter, then to the main panel.
The main panel (also called a consumer unit) splits power into circuits.
Each circuit has a breaker that trips if too much current flows.
Draw the path from pole to meter to panel to socket.
days.task: Draw the path of electricity from the street to a socket.
days.challenge: Explain to a friend what a circuit breaker does.

quiz.q: Where does electricity enter a home?
options: From the street main into a meter, then the main panel
quiz.explain: Power comes from the street through the meter into the main panel.

quiz.q: What does a circuit breaker do?
options: Trips off when too much current flows
quiz.explain: A breaker is a safety switch that cuts power when a circuit is overloaded.

quiz.q: What is the main panel also called?
quiz.explain: The consumer unit (main panel) splits power into separate circuits.

days.title: Safety First: Never Work Live
days.goal: Learn the safety rules that keep you alive around electricity.

video.title: How Electricity Works in Your House (From the Pole to Your Outlet)

steps: Rule one: always switch off the power at the panel before you touch wires.
Test with a voltage tester to prove the wires are dead.
Tell someone you are working on the power.
Never work with wet hands or standing in water.
days.task: Write your own five safety rules and stick them above your bench.
days.challenge: Prove a circuit is dead using a tester, twice.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to do before you touch any wires?
options: Switch off the power at the panel
quiz.explain: Always switch off the power at the panel before you touch wires.

quiz.q: How do you prove wires are dead?
quiz.explain: A voltage tester proves the wires are dead before you touch them.

quiz.q: What should you never do when working on electrics?
options: Work with wet hands or standing in water
Test the wires with a tester
quiz.explain: Never work with wet hands or standing in water.

days.title: Tools and Testers
days.goal: Know the tools: screwdrivers, strippers, testers and pliers.

video.title: How Electricity Works in Your House (From the Pole to Your Outlet)

steps: Lay out insulated screwdrivers, wire strippers, a voltage tester and pliers.
Learn that insulated tools have plastic handles that protect you.
Practise stripping a wire: remove about 1cm of plastic without cutting the copper.
Test a known live socket with the tester, then a dead one.
days.task: Strip ten wire ends cleanly without nicking the copper.
days.challenge: Strip a wire to exactly the right length first try.

quiz.q: Which tools do you need for electrical work?
options: Insulated screwdrivers, strippers, a tester and pliers
quiz.explain: Insulated screwdrivers, wire strippers, a voltage tester and pliers are the basic tools.

quiz.q: Why do insulated tools have plastic handles?
options: The plastic handles protect you from shocks
quiz.explain: Insulated handles protect you from electric shocks.

quiz.q: How much plastic should you strip off a wire?
quiz.explain: Strip about 1cm of plastic without cutting the copper inside.

days.title: Wires: Live, Neutral and Earth
days.goal: Tell the three wires apart by colour and job.

video.title: How to Wire a Light Switch

steps: Live (brown or red) brings power in; neutral (blue or black) carries it back.
Earth (green and yellow, or bare copper) is the safety wire.
The earth wire gives fault current a safe path to the ground.
Open a plug and name each wire inside.
days.task: Open a plug and label the live, neutral and earth wires.
days.challenge: Name the three wires and their colours without looking.

quiz.q: What does the live wire do?
quiz.explain: The live wire brings power into the circuit.

quiz.q: Which wire carries power back?
quiz.explain: The neutral wire carries power back to the supply.

quiz.q: What does the earth wire do?
options: Gives fault current a safe path to the ground
quiz.explain: Earth gives a fault a safe path away instead of through a person.

days.title: Wire a Light Switch
days.goal: Wire a simple one-way light switch on a practice board.

video.title: How to Wire a Light Switch

steps: Switch the power off and prove it is dead.
Connect the live wire to one side of the switch and the switched live to the other.
Connect the earth wire to the earth terminal.
Switch the power on and test the light.
days.task: Wire a working light switch on a practice board.
days.challenge: Wire the switch so it works first time.

quiz.q: Where does the live wire go on a light switch?
options: To one side of the switch
quiz.explain: The live wire connects to one side of the switch.

quiz.q: Where does the earth wire go on a light switch?
quiz.explain: The earth wire connects to the earth terminal.

quiz.q: What do you do after wiring a light switch?
options: Switch the power on and test the light
Cover the switch and walk away
quiz.explain: Switch the power on and test that the light works.

days.title: Switches: One-Way and Two-Way
days.goal: Know the difference between a switch that works from one place and from two places.

video.title: How to Wire a Light Switch

steps: A one-way switch controls a light from one spot.
A two-way switch lets two switches control the same light, like a hallway.
Learn the terminals: COM (common), L1 and L2.
Draw both switch circuits on paper.
days.task: Draw a one-way and a two-way switch circuit, labelled.
days.challenge: Explain two-way switching to a friend with a drawing.

quiz.q: What is a one-way switch?
options: A switch that works from one place
quiz.explain: One-way means one switch controls the light from one spot.

quiz.q: What is a two-way switch for?
options: Controlling one light from two places
quiz.explain: Two-way switching lets two switches control the same light.

quiz.q: What does COM mean on a switch?
quiz.explain: COM is the common terminal where the live wire connects.

days.title: Project: Wire a Practice Light Switch Board
days.goal: Build a small practice board with a switch and a bulb that works.

video.title: How to Wire an Electrical Outlet 2 Ways (Pigtails vs Daisy Chain)

steps: Fix a switch and a bulb holder to a board.
Run wires from the supply to the switch, then to the bulb.
Connect the earth wires together.
Test the board: switch on, bulb lights; switch off, bulb goes out.
days.task: Finish a working practice board with a switch and bulb.
days.challenge: Build the board with no loose wires showing.

quiz.q: What do you fix to the board first for a practice light switch board?
options: A switch and a bulb holder
quiz.explain: Fix a switch and a bulb holder to the board.

quiz.q: How do the wires run on a practice light switch board?
options: From the supply to the switch, then to the bulb
From the bulb to the supply
From the switch straight to the panel
In a ring back to the meter
quiz.explain: Wires run from the supply to the switch, then to the bulb.

quiz.q: How do you test a practice light switch board?
options: Switch on, the bulb lights; switch off, it goes out
quiz.explain: Switch on and the bulb should light; switch off and it should go out.

project.title: Wire a Practice Light Switch Board
project.brief: Build a board with a switch and bulb that works from the switch.
checks: Switch and bulb holder fixed firmly
Wires connected to the right terminals
Board neat and safe to handle

days.title: Connect Wires Safely
days.goal: Join wires with connectors so they stay tight and safe.

video.title: How to Wire an Electrical Outlet 2 Ways (Pigtails vs Daisy Chain)

steps: Strip the wire ends cleanly.
Twist the copper ends together, then screw on a wire connector.
Tug each wire to check it is tight.
Cover the joint with tape and tuck it into a box.
days.task: Make five wire joints that pass a tug test.
days.challenge: Make a joint so neat it fits inside a small box.

quiz.q: What do you do first when joining wires?
quiz.explain: Strip the wire ends cleanly first.

quiz.q: How do you join two wires with a connector?
options: Twist the copper ends together, then screw on a wire connector
Just tape them side by side
quiz.explain: Twist the copper ends together, then screw on a wire connector.

quiz.q: How do you check a wire joint is safe?
options: Tug each wire to check it is tight, then tape it and tuck it into a box
Pull it once and leave it open
quiz.explain: Tug each wire to check it is tight, cover the joint with tape and tuck it into a box.

days.title: Wire a Wall Socket
days.goal: Wire a wall socket (outlet) on a practice board.

video.title: How to Wire an Electrical Outlet 2 Ways (Pigtails vs Daisy Chain)

steps: Switch the power off and prove it dead.
Connect live to the brass screw, neutral to the silver screw, earth to the green screw.
Wrap each wire clockwise round its screw so tightening pulls it in.
Test the socket with a lamp or tester.
days.task: Wire a working socket on a practice board.
days.challenge: Wire a socket with all three wires on the right screws.

quiz.q: Which screw does the live wire go to in a wall socket?
quiz.explain: Live connects to the brass screw.

quiz.q: Which screw does the neutral wire go to in a wall socket?
quiz.explain: Neutral connects to the silver screw.

quiz.q: Which way should you wrap a wire round its screw?
options: Clockwise, so tightening pulls it in
quiz.explain: Wrap each wire clockwise round its screw so tightening pulls it in.

days.title: Pigtails and Daisy Chains
days.goal: Wire sockets two ways: pigtails and daisy chains.

video.title: How to Wire a One Way Light Switch

steps: A pigtail is a short wire that joins one socket to the main wires.
A daisy chain runs the main wires from one socket to the next.
Learn why pigtails are safer: one loose socket cannot kill the rest.
Practise both ways on a board with two sockets.
days.task: Wire two sockets with a pigtail and two with a daisy chain.
days.challenge: Explain why a pigtail is safer than a daisy chain.

quiz.q: What is a pigtail in socket wiring?
options: A short wire that joins one socket to the main wires
quiz.explain: A pigtail is a short wire that joins one socket to the main wires.

quiz.q: What is a daisy chain in socket wiring?
options: The main wires run from one socket to the next
quiz.explain: A daisy chain runs the main wires from one socket to the next.

quiz.q: Why are pigtails safer than a daisy chain?
options: One loose socket cannot kill the rest
quiz.explain: With pigtails, one loose socket cannot kill the rest of the circuit.

days.title: Wire a One-Way Switch Properly
days.goal: Wire a one-way switch neatly with the right cable.

video.title: How to Wire a One Way Light Switch

steps: Use twin and earth cable (two wires plus an earth in one sleeve).
Strip the outer sleeve without cutting the inner wires.
Connect live to COM and switched live to L1.
Neaten the cables with clips and test the switch.
days.task: Wire a one-way switch with neat clipped cables.
days.challenge: Wire it with no bare copper showing outside a terminal.

quiz.q: What cable do you use for a one-way switch?
quiz.explain: Use twin and earth cable: two wires plus an earth in one sleeve.

quiz.q: Where does the live wire go on a one-way switch?
quiz.explain: Connect live to COM and switched live to L1.

quiz.q: Where does the switched live go on a one-way switch?
quiz.explain: Connect the switched live to L1.

days.title: Test Your Socket Work
days.goal: Test sockets with a tester and fix common faults.

video.title: How to Wire a One Way Light Switch

steps: Plug a socket tester in and read the lights.
Learn what the lights mean: correct, no earth, live and neutral swapped.
Fix a swapped live and neutral by switching the wires.
Retest until the tester shows correct.
days.task: Test three sockets and fix any fault you find.
days.challenge: Find a swapped-wire fault from the tester lights alone.

quiz.q: What do you use to test a socket?
quiz.explain: Plug a socket tester in and read the lights.

quiz.q: What can a socket tester show you?
options: Correct wiring, no earth, or live and neutral swapped
quiz.explain: The lights mean correct, no earth, or live and neutral swapped.

quiz.q: How do you fix a socket with live and neutral swapped?
options: Switch the two wires round and retest
quiz.explain: Fix a swapped live and neutral by switching the wires, then retest until the tester shows correct.

days.title: Ring Circuits
days.goal: Understand a ring circuit: a loop of cable that feeds many sockets.

video.title: Ring Circuits Explained Step by Step

steps: A ring circuit is a loop that starts and ends at the panel.
The loop shares the load, so thinner cable can feed many sockets.
Learn that a break in the ring overloads the rest.
Draw a ring circuit feeding four sockets.
days.task: Draw a ring circuit with four sockets, labelled.
days.challenge: Explain why a ring must be a complete loop.

quiz.q: What is a ring circuit?
options: A loop of cable from the panel, through sockets, back to the panel
quiz.explain: A ring starts and ends at the panel, looping through the sockets.

quiz.q: Why is a ring circuit used for sockets?
options: The loop shares the load so many sockets can run safely
quiz.explain: The loop shares current between two paths, so more sockets can be fed.

quiz.q: What happens if a ring circuit breaks?
options: The rest of the ring can overload
quiz.explain: A break turns the ring into a radial, which can overload the cable.

days.title: Project: Wire a Socket Outlet on a Practice Board
days.goal: Wire two sockets on a board in a ring, and test them.

video.title: Ring Circuits Explained Step by Step

steps: Fix two sockets and a small panel to a board.
Run a ring of cable from the panel, through both sockets, back to the panel.
Connect every wire to the right terminal.
Test both sockets and check the ring is complete.
days.task: Finish a board with two working sockets in a ring.
days.challenge: Wire the ring with no faults on the tester.

quiz.q: What do you fix to the board for a socket outlet project?
options: Two sockets and a small panel
A switch and a bulb holder
quiz.explain: Fix two sockets and a small panel to a board.

quiz.q: How does the cable run in a ring socket project?
options: From the panel, through both sockets, back to the panel
From the panel to one socket only
From socket to socket in a straight line
From the meter to the bulb
quiz.explain: Run a ring of cable from the panel, through both sockets, back to the panel.

quiz.q: How do you finish a socket outlet project?
options: Test both sockets and check the ring is complete
Switch it on and walk away
quiz.explain: Test both sockets and check the ring is complete.

project.title: Wire a Socket Outlet on a Practice Board
project.brief: Wire two sockets in a ring on a board and test them.
checks: Sockets wired live, neutral and earth

days.title: Radial Circuits
days.goal: Understand a radial circuit: one cable run from the panel to the sockets.

video.title: Ring Circuits Explained Step by Step

steps: A radial circuit runs in one line from the panel to the last socket.
It is simpler than a ring and used for smaller loads.
Learn the limit: a radial feeds fewer sockets than a ring.
Draw a radial circuit feeding three sockets.
days.task: Draw a radial circuit with three sockets, labelled.
days.challenge: Explain when to use a radial instead of a ring.

quiz.q: What is a radial circuit?
options: One cable run from the panel to the sockets in a line
quiz.explain: A radial runs in one line from the panel to the last socket.

quiz.q: When is a radial circuit a good choice?
options: For a small number of sockets or a single load
quiz.explain: Radials suit small loads, like one room or a single cooker.

quiz.q: How is a radial different from a ring?
options: It does not loop back to the panel
quiz.explain: A radial ends at the last socket; a ring returns to the panel.

days.title: Lighting Circuits Part 1
days.goal: Learn how a lighting circuit is wired: loop-in and ceiling roses.

video.title: Radial Circuits Explained Step by Step

steps: A ceiling rose is the round fitting where the light hangs.
Learn the loop-in method: power loops from one light to the next.
Name the wires at a rose: live, neutral, earth and switched live.
Draw a lighting circuit with two lights.
days.task: Draw a lighting circuit with two ceiling roses, labelled.
days.challenge: Name every wire at a ceiling rose without looking.

quiz.q: What is a ceiling rose?
options: The round fitting where a light hangs
quiz.explain: The ceiling rose holds the light fitting and joins the circuit wires.

quiz.q: What is the loop-in method?
options: Power loops from one light to the next
quiz.explain: Loop-in runs the power cable from one ceiling rose to the next.

quiz.q: Which wires do you find at a ceiling rose?
options: Live, neutral, earth and switched live
quiz.explain: At a rose you find live, neutral, earth and switched live.

days.title: Lighting Circuits Part 2
days.goal: Wire a light with a switch using the loop-in method.

video.title: Radial Circuits Explained Step by Step

steps: Run cable from the panel to the first ceiling rose.
Loop the cable on to the second rose.
Run a switch cable down to the wall switch.
Test both lights from the switch.
days.task: Wire two lights on a practice board using loop-in.
days.challenge: Wire the lights so both switch on and off together.

quiz.q: Where does the cable go first in a lighting circuit?
options: From the panel to the first ceiling rose
From the switch to the panel
From the bulb to the socket
From the meter to the switch
quiz.explain: Run cable from the panel to the first ceiling rose.

quiz.q: How do you wire a second light in a loop-in circuit?
options: Loop the cable on to the second rose
Run a new cable from the panel
Join both lights to one switch wire
quiz.explain: Loop the cable on to the second rose.

quiz.q: How do you test a lighting circuit with two lights?
options: Test both lights from the switch
quiz.explain: Test both lights from the switch.

days.title: Lighting Circuits Part 3
days.goal: Add a second switch and fix lighting faults.

video.title: Radial Circuits Explained Step by Step

steps: Learn how two-way switching works on lights.
Wire a light with switches at two places.
Find a common fault: a light that stays on means a wrong switch wire.
Fix the fault and retest.
days.task: Wire a light controlled from two switches.
days.challenge: Find and fix a light that will not switch off.

quiz.q: How can two switches control one light?
quiz.explain: Two-way switching lets switches at two places control the same light.

quiz.q: What does it mean if a light stays on all the time?
options: The switch wires are wrong: live and switched live may be swapped
quiz.explain: A light stuck on usually means the switch wires are on the wrong terminals.

quiz.q: What do you do after fixing a lighting fault?
quiz.explain: Fix the fault and retest.

days.title: Project: Wire a Small Room Board
days.goal: Wire a practice board with a light and a socket, like a small room.

video.title: Lighting Circuits Part 1

steps: Plan the board: one light circuit and one socket circuit.
Wire the light with its switch, then the socket.
Keep the cables neat and clipped.
Test everything and fix any fault before you finish.
days.task: Finish a room board with a working light and socket.
days.challenge: Build the board with zero faults on first test.

quiz.q: What should your small room board plan include?
options: One light circuit and one socket circuit
quiz.explain: Plan the board: one light circuit and one socket circuit.

quiz.q: In what order do you wire a small room board?
options: Wire the light with its switch, then the socket
Wire the socket first, then the light switch
Wire both at the same time
quiz.explain: Wire the light with its switch, then the socket.

quiz.q: How do you finish a small room board?
options: Test everything and fix any fault before you finish
Cover the board and walk away
quiz.explain: Test everything and fix any fault before you finish.

days.title: Fuses and Breakers
days.goal: Know what fuses and breakers (MCBs) do and how to pick the right one.

video.title: Lighting Circuits Part 1

steps: An MCB is a switch that trips when too much current flows.
Learn the ratings: lights often use 6A, sockets 16A or 20A.
A bigger breaker does not mean safer; it must match the cable.
Practise resetting a tripped breaker safely.
days.task: Match three circuits to the right breaker size.
days.challenge: Explain why a 32A breaker on a lighting cable is dangerous.

quiz.q: What does an MCB do?
options: Trips off when too much current flows
quiz.explain: An MCB is a breaker that trips to protect the cable from overload.

quiz.q: What size MCB is often used for lights?
quiz.explain: Lighting circuits often use a 6A breaker.

quiz.q: Why must the breaker match the cable?
options: A breaker that is too big will not protect a thin cable
quiz.explain: A big breaker on a thin cable lets the cable overheat before tripping.

days.title: Install an MCB
days.goal: Fit a small breaker (MCB) into a practice panel safely.

video.title: Lighting Circuits Part 1

steps: Switch off the main power and prove it dead.
Clip the MCB onto the rail in the panel.
Connect the live wire to the MCB and the neutral to the neutral bar.
Switch on and test the circuit it feeds.
days.task: Fit an MCB that powers a practice circuit.
days.challenge: Fit the MCB with no loose wires in the panel.

quiz.q: What must you do before fitting an MCB?
options: Switch off the main power and prove it dead
quiz.explain: Switch off the main power and prove it dead first.

quiz.q: How is an MCB fitted into a panel?
options: Clip it onto the rail in the panel
quiz.explain: Clip the MCB onto the rail in the panel.

quiz.q: Where do the wires go when you fit an MCB?
options: Live to the MCB and neutral to the neutral bar
quiz.explain: Connect the live wire to the MCB and the neutral to the neutral bar.

project.title: Wire a Small Room Board
project.brief: Wire a board with a light, switch and socket like a small room.
checks: Light circuit works from its switch

days.title: Fault-Finding: No Power
days.goal: Find why a socket or light has no power, step by step.

video.title: Lighting Circuits Part 2

steps: Check the breaker first: is it tripped?
Check the bulb or appliance on a known good socket.
Test for power at the socket with your tester.
Work back along the circuit until you find the break.
days.task: Find the cause of a dead socket on a practice board.
days.challenge: Find a dead circuit fault in under ten minutes.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to check when a socket or light has no power?
quiz.explain: Check the breaker first: is it tripped?

quiz.q: How do you check if a bulb or appliance is faulty?
options: Try it on a known good socket
quiz.explain: Check the bulb or appliance on a known good socket.

quiz.q: How do you find where a circuit is broken?
options: Work back along the circuit until you find the break
Wait for it to fix itself
quiz.explain: Work back along the circuit until you find the break.

days.title: Fault-Finding: Tripping Breaker
days.goal: Find why a breaker keeps tripping.

video.title: Lighting Circuits Part 2

steps: A tripping breaker means overload or a short circuit.
Unplug everything, reset the breaker, then plug things back one by one.
The item that trips it again is the faulty one.
Check for damaged cables and water near sockets.
days.task: Find the faulty appliance that trips a breaker.
days.challenge: Tell an overload from a short circuit by the symptoms.

quiz.q: What does a tripping breaker mean?
options: The power is off for the day
quiz.explain: A tripping breaker means overload or a short circuit.

quiz.q: How do you find a faulty appliance that trips a breaker?
options: Unplug everything, reset, plug back one by one
quiz.explain: Plugging back one at a time shows which item trips the breaker.

quiz.q: What else should you check when a breaker keeps tripping?
options: Damaged cables and water near sockets
quiz.explain: Check for damaged cables and water near sockets.

days.title: Earth and Safety Checks
days.goal: Check earthing and bonding so a fault cannot shock anyone.

video.title: Lighting Circuits Part 2

steps: Earth wires must be joined firmly at every point.
Test that metal parts are connected to earth.
Learn that water pipes and gas pipes are bonded (joined) to earth.
Check the earth wire is never cut or missing.
days.task: Check the earthing on a practice board and record the result.
days.challenge: Explain why a missing earth wire is dangerous.

quiz.q: How should earth wires be joined?
quiz.explain: Earth wires must be joined firmly at every point.

quiz.q: What does bonding mean in electrical safety?
options: Joining water and gas pipes to earth
quiz.explain: Water pipes and gas pipes are bonded (joined) to earth.

quiz.q: What must never happen to an earth wire?
options: It must never be cut or missing
quiz.explain: Check the earth wire is never cut or missing.

days.title: Price a Small Electrical Job
days.goal: Price a small job from parts, time and a fair profit.

video.title: Lighting Circuits Part 3

steps: List the parts for a socket change and their prices.
Time the job and value your hours fairly.
Add 20 percent profit and round to a clean price.
Write a simple quote a customer can understand.
days.task: Write a clear quote for adding a socket, parts and labour shown.
days.challenge: Price a light fitting change fairly.

quiz.q: What is the first step in pricing a small electrical job?
options: List the parts and their prices
Ask the customer to pay anything
quiz.explain: List the parts for the job and their prices.

quiz.q: How do you price your time on a job?
options: Time the job and value your hours fairly
Charge by the colour of the wires
quiz.explain: Time the job and value your hours fairly.

quiz.q: How do you turn costs into a final price?
options: Add 20 percent profit and round to a clean price
quiz.explain: Add 20 percent profit and round to a clean price.

days.title: When to Call a Professional
days.goal: Know the jobs you must not do yourself.

video.title: Lighting Circuits Part 3

steps: Never work on the main supply cable or the meter.
Never work on a panel with the main power on.
Big new circuits and full rewires need a licensed electrician.
Know the rules in your area before you take paid work.
days.task: List five electrical jobs you must leave to a licensed electrician.
days.challenge: Explain to a customer why a job needs a licensed pro.

quiz.q: What electrical work must you never do yourself?
options: Work on the main supply cable or the meter
quiz.explain: Never work on the main supply cable or the meter.

quiz.q: When must you call a licensed electrician?
options: For big new circuits and full rewires
quiz.explain: Big new circuits and full rewires need a licensed electrician.

quiz.q: What should you check before taking paid electrical work?
quiz.explain: Know the rules in your area before you take paid work.

days.title: Test Your MCB Work
days.goal: Test an MCB installation safely before you call the job done.

video.title: Lighting Circuits Part 3

steps: Turn the power off and check the MCB is fitted tightly.
Turn the power on and test each circuit one at a time.
Press the test button on the MCB and check it trips.
Write down the test results for the customer.
days.task: Test an MCB board and record the results.
days.challenge: Test every circuit on a board without missing one.

quiz.q: What do you check before switching power back on after fitting an MCB?
options: The power is off and the MCB is fitted tightly
quiz.explain: Turn the power off and check the MCB is fitted tightly.

quiz.q: How do you test an MCB after fitting it?
options: Press the test button and check it trips
quiz.explain: Press the test button on the MCB and check it trips.

quiz.q: What should you do after testing an MCB installation?
options: Write down the test results for the customer
quiz.explain: Write down the test results for the customer.

days.title: Fault-Finding Practice: Dead Circuit
days.goal: Find why a circuit has no power, step by step.

video.title: How to Install an MCB in a Distribution Board

steps: Check the MCB has not tripped.
Check the socket with a tester.
Check the fuse in the plug.
Write down each check and what you found.
days.task: Find the fault in a dead circuit and write the steps you took.
days.challenge: Find a fault using only checks, no guessing.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to check when a socket has no power?
quiz.explain: A tripped breaker is the most common cause of a dead socket.

quiz.q: How do you find a faulty appliance that trips a breaker?
